title: Continual Model Routing in Evolving Model Hubs
claim: A router continually adapts to an evolving pool of models and dispatches each query to the best one, separate from execution.
layout: 2 shaded panels, left-to-right with time arrow, dashed boundaries, loop-back arrows
description: A two-region diagram on a blue (a) and orange (b) background with dashed borders. In (a), a Time arrow runs across the top above two dashed boxes: AI Hub (Day 1) with three colored AI icons, and AI Hub (Day i) with more models, separated by an ellipsis. A router icon labeled CARvE, drawn as a multi-directional arrow star, receives a Prompt from the bottom left. It sends solid arrows to one highlighted purple model, and dashed gray arrows point to the other models. caption: Conceptual framework for Continual Model Routing. (a) Given an evolving collection of AI models, our adaptive router CARvE learns continually from selection samples how to dynamically route a prompt query to the most appropriate model. (b) Actual execution of the model (not the focus of this paper).
abstract: AI model hubs provide access to a rapidly growing collection of powerful pre-trained models, enabling off-the-shelf mixture-of-experts systems with different routing strategies. However, this rapid growth poses two fundamental challenges: scaling model selection across thousands of experts and continually updating routing mechanisms as new models and tasks are introduced. In this paper, we formalise this setting as Continual Model Routing (CMR) and propose CMRBench, a new large-scale benchmark simulating realistic hub expansion and including over 2,000 candidate models. Finally, we introduce CARvE, a contrastive embedding approach for efficient continual model routing via checkpoint-based anchoring and structured replay. Extensive empirical results and ablations show that CARvE significantly outperforms zero-shot retrieval, fine-tuning, and adapter-merging baselines in model, family, and domain-level accuracy.
